title: Inband TACACS login must reach authorization and apply the returned roles

source_facts.claim: The release note describes authentication/accounting reaching ISE while an authorization request does not; conditions include mgmt0 down and an inband route/server source interface.
The Unit-test notes show mgmt0 down, Vlan150 up, inband Telnet login and `show user-account` roles; the comments label the role result as evidence the authorization packet was sent successfully.
The record says Cisco lab reproduction was not consistent, while the later verification comments identify a fix verification build and link a historical automation archive.

uncertainties: The customer report says lab reproduction was not consistent. The test must capture ISE live logs or an approved packet trace; successful authentication by itself cannot prove authorization receipt.
The exact transport is Telnet in the historical transcript; equivalent remote login transport may be used if it causes the same authorization flow.

behavior_validation.central_behavior: With the management interface unavailable and TACACS using the inband path, verify that a remote login reaches ISE authorization and the DUT applies the returned roles.
behavior_validation.intended_behavior: The bug-specific pass assertion should prove authorization request receipt at ISE and the expected roles on the remote account, in the inband/mgmt0-down condition.
behavior_validation.review_notes: The testcase defines required behavior and observable evidence; incidental reproduction details remain context unless required by the report.
behavior_validation.reported_failure: For the reported inband TACACS scenario, authentication/accounting traffic reaches ISE but its authorization request is reported not to reach ISE.
behavior_validation.observable_assertion: The relevant TACACS login uses the inband path while mgmt0 is down.; ISE logs or an approved capture proves the authorization request for this login reached the server.; DUT account evidence matches the roles returned by the ISE policy.

No assertion compares the DUT account roles with roles returned by ISE.
